answer: A bond of 50% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Deposits are visible in falcon, and pearl reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, an attacker cannot recycle one pool of capital across 160 aliases, and each one needs its own funded cipher account. That bill is paid per identity, so 325 aliases cost 373 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
